headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action hazards between Dify and Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read uploaded knowledge base files and write filesystem content, while Roo Code reads/writes VS Code workspace files and uses browser/MCP tools. A shared workspace or copied file path lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is plausible in default pair usage, though not proven universal.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or datastore path
IF one agent ingests the other agent's generated files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces and datastores for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before one agent reads the other's outputs
Use provenance labels on all inter-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem isolation at the orchestrator layer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, and Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots. Because both have broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, a shared workspace can expose sensitive files from one agent to the other or to external model APIs. The pairwise leakage path exists without special tooling, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF the two agents share any filesystem subtree containing sensitive files
IF either agent uploads file contents or screenshots to a remote model provider
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and separate secrets stores
Restrict sensitive files from both agents' readable paths
Turn off screenshot capture when not needed
Review outbound model-provider destinations before enabling them
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells; Roo Code also modifies git state and supports multiple instances via filesystem sharing, while Dify shares state via a server datastore. If they operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The overlap is dangerous by default when co-located, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to write the same directory or git checkout
IF Roo Code performs git operations while Dify writes files in the same tree
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Require explicit lock files for shared resources
Avoid git mutations from Roo Code on shared branches
requires-engineering: implement workspace locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Roo Code can act on code and browser tasks with approval-per-step. If Roo Code consumes Dify's output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected instruction can cascade into code edits, browser actions, or commits. The interaction is plausible and the downstream blast radius is large.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Dify-generated text as task instructions without verification
IF Dify output is forwarded into Roo Code's action prompts or tool inputs
mitigations: Require human review of Dify outputs before execution
Insert a verification step that checks Dify claims against source files
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for Dify-originated tasks
Tag Dify outputs as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific mismatch is evidenced. The only concrete compliance concern is that Dify handles conversation logs and knowledge base content while Roo Code handles source code and screenshots, which could matter if regulated data is placed into shared storage. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no breach is proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in a shared workspace or datastore
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Document retention settings for both deployments
Disable screenshot capture for regulated projects
Review where conversation logs are stored
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
